name: Fire as the primordial element and the 'ever-living Fire'
plain_explanation: Where Thales chose water and Anaximenes chose air, Heraclitus held fire to be the basic substance from which everything else, in a sense, borrows its existence, like flames feeding on fuel.
precise_definition: The doctrine that the cosmos 'was ever, is now, and ever shall be an ever-living Fire, with measures kindling and measures going out,' with fire's transformations ('first of all, sea; and half of the sea is earth, half whirlwind') generating the rest of the world.
why_it_mattered: Represents, alongside the Milesian choices of water and air, part of the sequence that Empedocles would later resolve by proposing all four (earth, air, fire, water) as co-equal elements.
examples: 'This world... was ever, is now, and ever shall be an ever-living Fire, with measures kindling and measures going out.'
competing_positions: Thales' water; Anaximenes' air; later, Empedocles' four co-equal elements
